title.value: Micron Reports Another Beat-and-Raise Earnings. The Stock Is Unchanged. -- Barrons.com

source_messages.body_text: By Adam Levine Memory-maker Micron Technology reported surging fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday afternoon as its memory chips continued to benefit from the artificial-intelligence boom. Its shares are up 1.6% in after-hours trading, after rising slightly in regular hours. Memory chips have long been a boom and bust industry. But Micron and competitors are trying to use the extreme demand for their chips in the AI revolution to produce more stable results over the long run. Adjusted earnings per share were $33.42, up from $3.03 last year, and ahead of Wall Street projections of $31.72. Revenue for the quarter reached $54 billion, above expectations of $51 billion, and up 379% on the year. Micron remains in uncharted territory. Pushed by demand for memory and storage chips for artificial-intelligence data centers, sales growth and profit margins are at all-time highs. "Industry demand has strengthened since our last earnings call, and we expect memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in fiscal 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026," said CEO Sanjay Mehrotra on the earnings call But what hasn't changed is Wall Street's skepticism about the durability of this unprecedented moment. Fiscal year 2027 began earlier this month, and Wall Street analysts expect $160 in adjusted earnings per share for Micron, which puts its forward price/earnings ratio at a low 6.6, well under the S&P 500's 18.5 P/E. Single-digit P/Es are nothing new for Micron. The reason is that memory is one of the most cyclical parts of the cyclical chip industry. There are wild swings in inventories and prices, which are reflected in fluctuating sales growth and gross profit margin for Micron. The old Wall Street maxim is that investors should buy these stocks when things go from bleak to merely terrible, and then sell when revenue growth and gross margin are peaking. Many tech investors still nurse the scars from a time when they mistimed the cycle, and they have one foot out the door during an upcycle. For the fourth quarter, Micron sailed past Wall Street expectations for sales growth and posted an eye-popping gross margin of 87%, all records for Micron. For those cautious investors, it doesn't take much imagination to think these are peak numbers, especially when Micron's guidance for the first quarter is for sales growth and gross margin to fall slightly. Data center investment is stretching past a trillion dollars a year, and all those AI servers require a lot of high-end memory and storage chips. There remains a severe shortage and prices have rocketed up at the fastest pace ever. The undersupply has bled into consumer tech, where 2026 price hikes have become the norm. In the past, upcycles tended to end when new factories opened, filling up depleted inventories. But that's been taking longer than usual. Because the down-cycle of 2022 and 2023 was so severe, Micron and the other memory giants-SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics-were reluctant to commit capital to expanding manufacturing capacity after the AI boom began with ChatGPT's release in November 2022. New factories aren't due to open until the middle of 2027, with more slated for the following years. Now, Micron and its peers are using their unusual market power to try to break the cycle. Micron is getting customers into five-year supply agreements, much more than the typical one-year deal. Unlike the usual memory contracts, these deals include a price floor and a very high ceiling, binding commitments, as well as customer deposits. Last quarter, Micron devoted much of the scripted portion of the earnings call to detailing these agreements, which it hopes will soften the eventual down-cycle. There were 16 customer contracts that covered roughly 20% of its memory chip volume and a third of storage chips. The company is betting that less cyclical financials will lead to a rerating from its single-digit P/E. But Micron may have to show that new pattern before it gets any credit. The day after the last earnings report, analysts raced each other to raise their fiscal year 2027 financial estimates and price targets, and the stock was up 16%. But shares have since faded, as the usual skepticism has bled back in. Meanwhile, Micron is using its unprecedented cash flow to reshape its balance sheet. Micron had $59 billion in free cash flow in the just completed fiscal year. The company repaid $10 billion in debt, now down to $5 billion, and has begun a share-repurchase program. Wall Street expects $129 billion in free cash flow for the new fiscal year. Write to Adam Levine at adam.levine@barrons.com This content was created by Barron's, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. Barron's is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal. title.value: Stock Market Today: Dow Knocked Down, Nasdaq Pares Gain; Micron Holds Firm After Earnings Soar -- IBD

source_messages.body_text: By David Saito-Chung And Scott Lehtonen The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished Wednesday's session lagging other major stock indexes, as cooler-than-expected inflation data lifted at least some of the market. Micron Technology came into focus ahead of earnings reported after the close, while medical stock Liquidia took a bludgeoning on the stock market today over a patent dispute. All session long, the Dow twisted and turned around the break-even level before eventually dropping nearly 0.9% to end at 50,906. The S&P 500 slipped in the final minutes of the day, finishing down nearly 0.3% at 7,651. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite early in the session moved up 0.5%, then revved that advance to 0.8% before seeing its gain shrink to 0.2% in the final hour, closing at 26,861. It marked a session high of 27,108 and moved not far off that level. Small caps initially joined the advance during the final day of the third quarter, but the Russell 2000 index surrendered early gains of 0.5% to lose 0.4%. The S&P MidCap 400 also sold off in the final hour of regular trading. It lost 0.6% to end at 3,596. The S&P 400 still holds a gain of 8.8% since Jan. 1. Yet the benchmark for midcap stocks is also facing an important test of support at its rising 200-day moving average. West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures rose more than 1% to roughly $90.65 a barrel. The 10-year Treasury yield had dropped to as low as 5.2% before rebounding to finish at 5.29%. Also, bitcoin surrendered early gains to finish fractionally lower at $83,566. MICRON EARNINGS AFTER THE CLOSE In the memory chip space, all eyes still focused on Micron Technology with earnings reported after the close. The Boise, Idaho-based company, currently forming a new base, edged 3 cents higher to 1,065 during the regular session and hit a session high of 1,083.50. At that high, Micron traded less than 14% below the current cup pattern's left-side high of 1,255. After the close, the stock seesawed between small gains and small losses and showed a bid of around $1,067. The company posted adjusted earnings of $33.42 a share, up more than tenfold vs. a year ago. Revenue soared 380% to $54.23 billion. Micron also forecast earnings of $38.15 per share, plus or minus $1, for the November-ending fiscal first quarter of fiscal year 2027. Expectations for huge growth in the just-ended August quarter include a consensus forecast of $31.72 per share, up tenfold from $3.03 in the year-ago quarter. Analysts surveyed by FactSet also project sales to rise 354% to $51.3 billion. Watch for updates on the earnings and news from Micron's conference call at Investor's Business Daily's Technology section. ANALYSIS OF THE TREASURY BOND SELL-OFF While the core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index for August showed a smaller than expected rise of 0.2% vs. the prior month and a 3% year-over-year rise, the selling of long-dated U.S. Treasurys continued. The yield on the key 10-year bond rose to as high as 5.30% before settling at 5.29%, up nearly 4 basis points. The two-year note finished the session with a yield of 4.89%, up three-fourths of one full percentage point for the month. It was the largest one-month rise in yield since February 2023, according to Dow Jones Data. The money management firm Cypress Capital sees two major factors in understanding the recent sharp rise in the cost of long-term borrowing. "The rise in Treasury yields has been driven predominantly by real yields rather than higher market-implied inflation expectations. Two potential sources of pressure make the near-term path for yields especially uneasy," Mark Dodson of Cypress Capital wrote in comments emailed to IBD. "Hedge funds have begun reducing exposure to the Treasury basis trade, potentially removing buyers of cash Treasurys." Cypress also noted caution on buying the dip in Treasury bonds for another reason: the Japanese yen continues to fall despite efforts by both the Japanese government and the U.S. Treasury to support the currency. "If yen weakness resumes in earnest, (U.S.) Treasury's concern is that it could add to the pressure on U.S. yields. Taken together, these developments offer no obvious route back to lower yields soon." 3:45 p.m. ET STOCK MARKET TODAY: LIQUIDIA HAMMERED Within the medical space, Liquidia plummeted 54% in massive volume after a federal judge ruled against the company's motion to block a portion of claims related to patents held by United Therapeutics. Trading in Liquidia spiked to more than 16 million shares, or more than one-sixth of the stock's total 90 million shares outstanding. The company has a float, or freely traded shares, of 78 million. Liquidia, which has developed technology that improves the efficacy and usage of inhaled medicines, said it would proceed with an appeal regarding United Therapeutics' claim that its patent covering the use of inhaled treprostinil to treat a specific form of pulmonary hypertension was infringed. The stock was in the middle of forming a new base until Wednesday's price collapse. Now the stock has deeply undercut its long-term 200-day moving average and is testing lows last seen in March. Shares of United Therapeutics, which has a low Relative Strength Rating of 38 on a scale of 1 to 99, shot more than 14% higher. The stock also climbed back above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. More work is needed to develop the right side of a new base. 2:28 p.m. ET LOSERS EDGE OUT WINNERS Breadth in the stock market today was not ideal. Losers slightly edged winners on the Nasdaq exchange by a narrow margin of 30 stocks; on the New York Stock Exchange, declining issues outpaced gainers by a 4-3 margin. Looking at Investor's Business Daily's 142 key industry groups, top performers included scientific and measuring electronics firms, education, oil refining, security software and medical software. The Big Picture: These 3 Chip Gear Plays Total $1 Trillion In Market Cap Also up were oil-and-gas drillers, design software makers, telecom consumer products, gaming and internet content. These groups and a few others rallied 1.5% or more on a market-cap-weighted basis. With the month of September and the third quarter drawing to a close, turnover jacked 30% higher vs. the same time Tuesday on the Nasdaq. On the NYSE, volume ran 7% higher. Further, among exchange traded funds, the Invesco QQQ ETF tacked on 0.7% and the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF rose 0.3%. CYBERSECURITY STOCKS AT NEW HIGHS Within the strengthening enterprise software space, Palo Alto Networks stood out. The megacap tech rose more than 3% and marked an all-time high of 404.69. Volume ran 4% above usual levels. Palo Alto also crossed a 398.88 buy point in a seven-week cup-style base that showed a bit of the contours of the double-bottom pattern. The intraday high of 387.33 set on Aug. 27 could be viewed as an early buy point. Tech industry observers said in recent weeks that reports of frontier artificial-intelligence models escaping test environments indicate the growing need for security software to protect data and digital networks. Analysts polled by FactSet see Santa Clara, Calif.-based Palo Alto posting a 4% increase in earnings per share to 97 cents in the fiscal first quarter ending in October on a 34% bulge in sales to $3.31 billion. Palo Alto's sales have almost tripled -- reaching $11.48 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended this past July -- from $4.26 billion in the fiscal year ended in July 2020. Earnings per share almost quadrupled, to $3.84 from $1.02, over the same time frame. Fiscal 2027 profit growth is seen slowing, however, to 9%, coming in at $4.19 a share. Palo Alto has a $317.7 billion market value with 818 million shares outstanding. Group mate CrowdStrike is extended from its rebound off the rising 10-week moving average near 197.54 during the week ended Aug. 28. CrowdStrike stock rose more than 1% and has gained 5.5% for the week so far. The first and second tests of the 10-week moving average following a successful breakout from a good base offer new chances to buy shares or add to a winning core holding. 1:07 p.m. ET DATA CENTER, STORAGE FIRMS EXCEL NetApp continued to show leadership on the stock market today. Shares rose more than 1%, with gains exceeding 5% for the week. As seen on a weekly chart, the stock showed a very wild reversal in the week ended Sept. 4. But it was a bullish reversal. After falling as much as 14% during that week to a low of 161, buyers bought with force and NetApp finished the week well off the low and down only 0.8%. Heavy weekly volume that week signified a major shakeout of weak shareholders. Since then, the expert in data storage and data management products has rebounded with strength while maintaining bullish support at or near its rising 10-week moving average. Trading near 212, the stock is outside the 5% buy zone from the cup with handle and a 199.62 buy point; watch for a potential mild pullback into the proper buying area. The 5% buy zone goes up to 219.51. NetApp has recently expanded into a full-size position on Leaderboard. The initial entry on the model stock portfolio was on Monday at 203.58. Also within the data center and data storage space, Sandisk edged higher. Trading near 1,737, the stock is holding above key moving averages, including a rising 50-day line and the shorter-term 21-day exponential moving average. Sandisk remains in basing mode. Industry mate Western Digital rose nearly 2%. But at 461.58, the stock is still below its own downward-sloping 50-day moving average. Stocks with strong fundamentals, heavy institutional ownership, and gains above the 50-day line, not below, tend to lead new uptrends in the stock market today and are often the first to break out to new highs. 11:40 a.m. ET STOCK MARKET TODAY: MICROSOFT FLEXES ITS MUSCLES (MORE TO FOLLOW) Dow Jones Newswires September 30, 2026 16:55 ET (20:55 GMT) Copyright (c) 2026 Dow Jones & Company, Inc. title.value: Micron Reports Another Beat-and-Raise Earnings. The Stock Is Unchanged. -- Barrons.com

source_messages.body_text: By Adam Levine Memory-maker Micron Technology reported surging fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday afternoon as its memory chips continued to benefit from the artificial-intelligence boom. Its shares are up 1.6% in after-hours trading, after rising slightly in regular hours. Memory chips have long been a boom and bust industry. But Micron and competitors are trying to use the extreme demand for their chips in the AI revolution to produce more stable results over the long run. Adjusted earnings per share were $33.42, up from $3.03 last year, and ahead of Wall Street projections of $31.72. Revenue for the quarter reached $54 billion, above expectations of $51 billion, and up 379% on the year. Micron remains in uncharted territory. Pushed by demand for memory and storage chips for artificial-intelligence data centers, sales growth and profit margins are at all-time highs. "Industry demand has strengthened since our last earnings call, and we expect memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in fiscal 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026," said CEO Sanjay Mehrotra on the earnings call But what hasn't changed is Wall Street's skepticism about the durability of this unprecedented moment. Fiscal year 2027 began earlier this month, and Wall Street analysts expect $160 in adjusted earnings per share for Micron, which puts its forward price/earnings ratio at a low 6.6, well under the S&P 500's 18.5 P/E. Single-digit P/Es are nothing new for Micron. The reason is that memory is one of the most cyclical parts of the cyclical chip industry. There are wild swings in inventories and prices, which are reflected in fluctuating sales growth and gross profit margin for Micron. The old Wall Street maxim is that investors should buy these stocks when things go from bleak to merely terrible, and then sell when revenue growth and gross margin are peaking. Many tech investors still nurse the scars from a time when they mistimed the cycle, and they have one foot out the door during an upcycle. For the fourth quarter, Micron sailed past Wall Street expectations for sales growth and posted an eye-popping gross margin of 87%, all records for Micron. For those cautious investors, it doesn't take much imagination to think these are peak numbers, especially when Micron's guidance for the first quarter is for sales growth and gross margin to fall slightly. Data center investment is stretching past a trillion dollars a year, and all those AI servers require a lot of high-end memory and storage chips. There remains a severe shortage and prices have rocketed up at the fastest pace ever. The undersupply has bled into consumer tech, where 2026 price hikes have become the norm. In the past, upcycles tended to end when new factories opened, filling up depleted inventories. But that's been taking longer than usual. Because the down-cycle of 2022 and 2023 was so severe, Micron and the other memory giants-SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics-were reluctant to commit capital to expanding manufacturing capacity after the AI boom began with ChatGPT's release in November 2022. New factories aren't due to open until the middle of 2027, with more slated for the following years. Now, Micron and its peers are using their unusual market power to try to break the cycle. Micron is getting customers into five-year supply agreements, much more than the typical one-year deal. Unlike the usual memory contracts, these deals include a price floor and a very high ceiling, binding commitments, as well as customer deposits. "These multi-year take-or-pay agreements sharpen our long-term supply planning and enhance the durability and predictability of our strong financial performance," said Mehrotra on the call. Last quarter, Micron devoted much of the scripted portion of the earnings call to detailing these agreements, which it hopes will soften the eventual down-cycle. Now there are 36 such agreements-up from 16-covering about a third of Micron's revenue through 2030. The company is betting that less cyclical financials will lead to a rerating from its single-digit P/E. But Micron may have to show that new pattern before it gets any credit. The day after the last earnings report, analysts raced each other to raise their fiscal year 2027 financial estimates and price targets, and the stock was up 16%. But shares have since faded, as the usual skepticism has bled back in. Meanwhile, Micron is using its unprecedented cash flow to reshape its balance sheet. Micron had $59 billion in free cash flow in the just completed fiscal year. The company repaid $10 billion in debt, now down to $5 billion, and has begun a share-repurchase program. Wall Street expects $129 billion in free cash flow for the new fiscal year. Write to Adam Levine at adam.levine@barrons.com This content was created by Barron's, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. source_messages.body_text: By Ed Carson Dow Jones futures edged higher after hours, along with S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq futures. Micron Technology earnings beat late Wednesday while Google released a new cutting-edge AI model. The stock market rally was mixed Wednesday as Treasury yields hit new long-term highs and crude oil prices rose. The Nasdaq rose but closed well off highs, while the other indexes declined. Hewlett Packard Enterprise broke out on bullish guidance and a hefty order for its systems featuring Advanced Micro Devices new Helios AI rack system and chips. Palo Alto Networks, Snowflake and Microsoft also flashed buy signals on a strong day for software and megacaps. Micron stock is on the Leaderboard watchlist. Microsoft and Palo Alto stock are on SwingTrader. Snowflake stock, AMD, Microsoft and Micron are on the IBD 50. Microsoft and AMD stock are on the IBD Big Cap 20. The video embedded in the article reviews Wednesday's market action and analyzes HPE stock, Snowflake and Microsoft. It also takes an early peek at Micron following earnings. DOW JONES FUTURES TODAY Dow Jones futures edged higher. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.1%. Nasdaq-100 futures rose 0.2%. Remember that overnight action in Dow futures and elsewhere doesn't necessarily translate into actual trading in the next regular stock market session. MICRON EARNINGS Micron Technology earnings and revenue skyrocketed, both beating fiscal Q4 views. The memory-chip giant also guided higher. Micron stock rose slightly in overnight action. Shares were essentially flat at 1,065.11 in Wednesday's session, continuing to pause bullishly. MU stock would be actionable above its quasi-handle around 1,1108. Micron has a cup base with a 1,255 buy point. OTHER MEMORY STOCKS Flash memory giant Sandisk, South Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix and hard-drive firm Seagate Technology all edged higher in extended action. All are trading close to potential buy points. Join IBD experts as they analyze leading stocks and the market on IBD Live STOCK MARKET RALLY The stock market rally was mixed Wednesday. The indexes started higher, led by the Nasdaq. Core PCE inflation cooled more than expected, but that was largely due to methodology changes. Long-term Treasury yields reversed higher, with the indexes mixed, closing near session lows. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.9% in Wednesday's stock market trading. The S&P 500 index fell 0.25%, just holding the 50-day line. The Nasdaq composite climbed 0.2%. The small-cap Russell 2000 lost 0.4%. Google parent Alphabet, Apple, Amazon.com and Microsoft all rose about 1%, with Nvidia up 0.5%. All five are Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite giants. After the close, Google stock rose slightly on the release of Gemini 4 Argon, its most advanced AI model. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF declined 0.7%. The Direxion Nasdaq-100 Equal Weighted ETF retreated 0.2%. It was a good day for software stocks beyond Microsoft. Palo Alto popped 2.3% to 397.31 and Snowflake stock rose 2.8% to 399.56. PANW topped a 398.88 consolidation buy point intraday while SNOW stock extended a 50-day line bounce, broke a trendline and tested the bulk of several weeks of tight trading. HPE stock jumped 3.9% to 63.89, breaking out past a cup-with-handle buy point of 63.44 but closing near session lows. The server giant got a big order from Vultr for HPE systems using AMD racks and processors, and raised networking revenue guidance. Chips and AI plays were mixed, aside from HPE. CRUDE OIL PRICES, TREASURY YIELDS U.S. crude oil prices rose 1.2% to $90.42 a barrel, surging 30.1% in Q3. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed nearly four basis points to 5.29%, up 87 basis points in Q3. It hit 5.31% intraday, the highest since 2002. The two-year Treasury yield, more closely tied to the Fed rate outlook, was little changed at 4.885%. The odds of an October Fed rate hike fell to 37% vs. 50.9% on Tuesday and 70.9% on Sept. 23. ETFS Among growth ETFs, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF gained 1.2%, with Palo Alto and Microsoft major components. The VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF climbed 0.35%, with Nvidia stock, AMD and Micron major positions. ARK Innovation ETF lost 0.4% and ARK Genomics ETF rose 0.5%. SPDR S&P Metals & Mining ETF fell 0.3%. The Energy Select SPDR ETF lost a fraction and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund gave up 1.35%. The Industrial Select Sector SPDR Fund sank 1.3% and the Financial Select SPDR ETF retreated 1.1%. Best Growth Stocks To Buy And Watch WHAT TO DO NOW Techs are doing fairly well, with a variety of stocks showing strength. The Micron earnings reaction will be important for chips and AI. But outside of tech, the market is struggling. That divergence is worrisome. Investors can make buys but be ready to exit positions that don't work out. If super-nimble trading isn't your style, it's OK to hold more cash. Do work on watchlists. Read The Big Picture every day to stay in sync with the market direction and leading stocks and sectors. title.value: Micron 4Q Profit, Revenue Surge as Memory Crunch Looks to Last Through 2028 -- Update

source_messages.body_text: By Elias Schisgall Micron Technology profit and revenue surged in the fiscal fourth quarter, as the company said the shortage of memory chips that has propelled its explosive growth in the past year shows no signs of slowing down. "Industry demand has strengthened since our last earnings call, and we expect memory and storage supply demand conditions to be much tighter in fiscal 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026," Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said on a Wednesday call with analysts. Mehrotra's comments come as investors have debated the durability of the memory shortage that has fueled Micron's blowout earnings. In June, he told analysts that the memory crunch would last past 2027, but struck somewhat of a softer tone than he did on Wednesday. Micron has been working to boost its production capacity for memory, and Mehrotra said several fabs are on track to start production over the next two years. Still, the magnitude of the supply imbalance, especially for a type of memory called DRAM, means that Micron will need to increase its capital expenditures in the new fiscal year, he said. The company guided for around $25 billion in capital expenditures in the first half of the fiscal year, including about $11.5 billion in the first quarter. Capital spending is expected to rise further in the second half of the year. Most of the increased spending is expected to go toward construction, the company said. "We are focused on our global manufacturing expansions to help address customer demand growth through the end of this decade and beyond," Mehrotra said. The company also disclosed that it had signed 26 long-term supply agreements with customers looking to lock up their share of the scarce memory chips, up from 16 in June, and totaling $32 billion in financial commitments. Some of those agreements extend into 2031, Mehrotra said, and they together represent more than 35% of the company's expected revenue through 2030. Micron on Wednesday reported a profit of $37.7 billion, or $32.87 a share, in the quarter ended Sept. 3, up from $3.2 billion, or $2.83 a share, a year earlier. On an adjusted basis, earnings were $33.42 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet were projecting $31.72 a share. Revenue rose sharply to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year prior. Analysts were expecting $51.33 billion in revenue. For the current first quarter, Micron is projecting adjusted earnings of between $37.15 and $39.15 a share on revenue of $60 billion to $63 billion. Analysts currently expect $35.47 a share in adjusted earnings on $57.4 billion in revenue. Shares were down 0.8% at $1,057.00 in after-hours trading on Wednesday.
